title: MSFS 2024 VR Clarity Test: A220 Glass Cockpit on Pimax Crystal Light
description:
Can you run four massive 15-inch glass cockpit displays in native VR resolution without sacrificing smooth frame rates or touching the zoom button?

In this video, we put the Airbus A220 (by Synaptic / iniBuilds) through its paces in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 using the Pimax Crystal Light headset. We test gauge clarity, text readability, night lighting immersion, and real-world performance using Medium settings with live FSLTL traffic injected.

✈️Flight & setup details
• Aircraft: Airbus A220 (Synaptic Simulations / iniBuilds)
• Departure: Toulouse-Blagnac Airport (LFBO), France
• VR Headset: Pimax Crystal Light
• GPU: Nvidia GeForce RTX 4090
• CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9800X3D
• Memory: 64GB DDR5
• Sim & Settings: MSFS 2024 (Sim Update 6) | Medium Graphics Preset
• Traffic: FSLTL Live Traffic Injection

📋What we cover
• VR readability of small pedestal switches and 15" glass displays without zooming
• SimBrief flight plan import workflow & EFB performance calculations
• Automated smart checklist behavior
• Daytime vs. night lighting immersion in VR
• Real-world VR frame rates (40–45 FPS target) and flight handling
• VR control tips (mouse vs. hardware vs. upcoming voice control)
